LESSON: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON- FICTION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction, part of Strand 11 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: what he or she has read about. 1. What is the importance of reading widely? 2. What do you consider when selecting a reading text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. skim through print and electronic reading materials on careers,

2. discuss the general ideas with peers,

3. scan print and electronic reading materials and identify key words and phrases,

4. use a dictionary to look up the meaning of vocabulary acquired during independent reading,

5. read various texts on risky behaviour by road users and note the key points,

6. share with peers

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. skim through print and electronic reading materials on careers,
2. discuss the general ideas with peers,
3. scan print and electronic reading materials and identify key words and phrases,
4. use a dictionary to look up the meaning of vocabulary acquired during independent reading,
5. read various texts on risky behaviour by road users and note the key points,
6. share with peers

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner selects reading materials to enhance their ability to make decisions.

• Learning to learn: It is achieved as the learner manages time while silently and reading varied materials.

Values:
Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner engages in the selection of reading material.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills education: It is promoted as the learner applies decision making skills while choosing materials to read

extensively.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The skill of extensive reading is relevant in all subjects including Integrated Science and Pre-Technical Studies.
